[FACT] User has been using a smoker box on their gas grill a lot lately.  
[PREFERENCE] User is looking for meats that would be perfect for smoking.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant recommended brisket, pulled pork, ribs, tri-tip, sausages, burnt ends, and pork belly as excellent choices for smoking.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant advised to keep the smoker temperature low (around 225-250°F) and to use wood chips like hickory, apple, or cherry for different flavor profiles.  
[PREFERENCE] User is interested in trying out new types of wood chips for smoking.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant provided a breakdown of flavors for hickory, apple, and cherry wood chips, including their pairing suggestions.  
[FACT] User has tried using hickory chips for the first time and was impressed by the flavor.  
[FACT] User has purchased bags of applewood and mesquite chips.  
[PREFERENCE] User is looking for recommendations on how to store wood chips to keep them fresh.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant recommended storing wood chips in airtight containers, keeping them in a dry place, maintaining cool temperatures, ensuring they are dry before storage, using them within 6-12 months, freezing for longer storage, and labeling containers.  
[PREFERENCE] User is considering trying to smoke a whole turkey or pork belly.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant provided tips for smoking a whole turkey, including brining, choosing the right wood, temperature control, and using a meat thermometer.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant provided tips for smoking pork belly, including curing, scoring the fat, using robust wood, low and slow cooking, and resting the meat.
